newsitem.title: ERITREA: Australian firms to bid for Eritrea gold.
newsitem.headline: Australian firms to bid for Eritrea gold.

text.p: Australian United Gold NL and Kalgoorlie Mine Management Pty will participate in the second round of bidding for mining concessions in Eritrea, an official said on Tuesday.

Estephanos Oqubazghi, representative of the companies in the Eritrean capital of Asmara, told Reuters in an interview: "They are putting in a joint bid for a prospecting concession in the Augaro area in the western lowlands."

In the first round of bidding completed early this year, seven companies were granted concessions, mainly in the central highland plateau around Asmara. They included U.S. concern Phelps Dodge Exploration Corp, Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Company Ltd and Canada's Rift Resources Ltd.

Others were Australia's WMC (Overseas) Pty Ltd, U.S.-based Canadian company Golden Star Resources-Pan African Resources Corporation, Franco-Australian company LaSource Development SAS and Canada's Ophir Ventures Inc.
Australian United Gold and Kalgoorlie Mine Management made separate bids in the first round but were unsuccessful.
"Australian United Gold applied for an exploration license on the plateau around Asmara. Kalgoorlie Mine Management applied for a prospecting license in the west," Estephanos said.
For the second round commencing later this year, the western lowlands of Eritrea will be opened up for bidding.

"We have seven delineated areas in the western lowlands and two in the eastern lowlands close to the coast. These will be open for exploration licenses," said Asmarom Mesfin, head of mining administration at energy, mines and water resources ministry in Asmara.
"Apart from that, bidders can select other areas for prospecting," Asmarom told Reuters.
Australian United Gold and Kalgoorlie Mine Management will now enter a joint bid for a prospecting license in the western lowlands around Augaro. Both companies are looking for gold.
Eritrea became independent from Ethiopia in 1993.
It published a mining proclamation in March 1995 when several mining companies had already submitted proposals.
The first round of bidding for concessions started later in 1995 and was completed in early 1996.
Eritrea has a history of mining. Italy, which colonised Eritrea between 1890 and 1940, had companies mining around Asmara in the 1930s and 1940s.
"According to Italian literature, they were mainly interested in gold before the Second World War," said Asmarom.
Japanese companies were mining for copper in Eritrea during the 1960s and 1970s but left the country when a civil war in the then northern Ethiopian province intensified.
